newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Gaddafi criticises Kuwait over women vote.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi criticises Kuwait over women vote.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Tuesday attacked Kuwait for not allowing women to vote in parliamentary elections.

"Banning women from being candidates and from voting at elections for the Kuwaiti parliament...does not reinforce Kuwait's freedom, but on the contrary, it weakens it...," the official Libyan news agency JANA quoted Gaddafi as saying.
"It harms Kuwait which is still threatened in its independence," he added.
Gaddafi earlier this year upset Kuwait when he said during a visit in Cairo that Kuwait should not be independent if it could not defend itself.
JANA, received in Tunis, said Gaddafi made the statement at the city of Sirte where he attended a meeting of Libya's grassroots popular committees.
Kuwait held on Monday its second parliamentary elections since the 1991 Gulf War when a U.S.-led multinational force ended a seven month Iraqi occupation of the oil-rich country.
